title: As AI Networks Scale In Three Directions, So Does Arista
gist: Arista Networks posted its first $3 billion quarter (Q2 2026 revenue +37.7 percent to $3.04 billion, net income 40 percent of sales) and raised full-year 2026 guidance by $1.1 billion to $12.6 billion, with deferred revenue up 69 percent and customer purchase commitments up 2.7X as prepayments fund component procurement. The author frames Arista's growth as riding three distinct AI network directions — scale up, scale out and scale across — where scale across is already a $3 billion switch plus $1 billion optics market in 2026 heading to $15 billion plus $5 billion by 2030, while the scale up opportunity is gated on customers displacing Nvidia's NVLink/NVSwitch.

themes.theme: Q2 2026 print and the $3 billion threshold

insights.claim: Arista Networks crossed $3 billion in quarterly sales for the first time in Q2 2026, with revenue up 37.7 percent year on year to $3.04 billion and 12.1 percent sequential growth from Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 12 percent sequential step in a quarter of alleged supply tightness marks acceleration, not plateau — the AI networking cycle has not yet rolled over.
insights.locator: Add it all up, and revenues for the company

insights.claim: Arista Networks product revenues rose 38.8 percent to $2.61 billion in the June 2026 quarter, with growth spread across essentially all product lines and segment categories rather than concentrated in one AI line.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Broad-based growth reduces the single-customer/single-product concentration risk usually discounted into AI-levered networking names.
insights.locator: In the second quarter ended in June

insights.claim: Arista Networks' operating income grew 39.7 percent to $1.38 billion and net income grew 36.5 percent to $1.21 billion in Q2 2026, holding net margin at roughly 40 percent of revenue despite a component-constrained supply chain.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Margin has not been given up to buy components — pricing power is intact, so watch for the first quarter where net margin slips below 40 percent as the leading indicator of cost pass-through failure.
insights.locator: Operating income was up 39.7 percent

insights.claim: Networking suppliers convert prepaid backlog into supply-chain advantage: customer cash paid up front gives visibility to plan component purchasing and factory operations, and the vendors that outbid rivals for wafers, packaging and memory are the ones that grow revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Treat deferred revenue and purchase commitments as the real forward indicator for AI hardware names — they are a claim on scarce components, not just an accounting artifact.
insights.quote: If they pay more for the components, and they pay more, they get more.
insights.locator: With companies like Arista Networks, they build up a revenue backlog

insights.claim: Arista Networks ended June 2026 with $6.87 billion in deferred revenues, up 69 percent year on year, and $9.7 billion in customer purchase commitments, up 2.7X year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Purchase commitments growing 2.7X while revenue grows 38 percent means the forward book is expanding far faster than the P&L — revenue guidance is likely to keep being revised up.
insights.locator: The company had $6.87 billion in deferred revenues

insights.claim: The deferred revenue build in the current AI buildout is visibly larger than the equivalent spike during the cloud buildout of the 2010s, according to a chart the company presented to Wall Street analysts.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The company itself is framing AI as a bigger cycle than cloud — useful for sizing the eventual air pocket when deferred revenue rolls over.
insights.quote: This AI spike here in the 2020s is obviously much larger than the cloud spike a decade ago.
insights.locator: In the call going over the financial results with Wall Street analysts

insights.claim: Arista Networks held $13.34 billion in cash and equivalents at the end of June 2026, up 50.9 percent year on year, giving it room to make tactical or strategic acquisitions and to maneuver in a tight supply chain.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A $13 billion war chest makes Arista a plausible acquirer in optics or scale-up silicon — watch adjacent private assets for takeout premia.
insights.locator: Equally important to revenue and profit growth is cash and equivalents

insights.claim: The raised 2026 guidance is probably conservative, with management holding back upside that will be crystallized later for effect rather than recognized now.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Implies positive guidance revisions remain the base case into H2 2026 — beats-and-raises, not a one-time reset.
insights.quote: There is a chance that Arista Networks can beat this number by a little bit and is saving some upside that is a little fuzzy today that will crystalize later for dramatic effect.
insights.locator: Those who do well at this game can grow their revenues

themes.theme: Software and subscription attach as the sticky layer

insights.claim: Arista Networks' services revenues rose 31.3 percent to $430.5 million in Q2 2026, carried by adoption of the EOS network operating system plus CloudVision, LANZ, Path Tracer, DANZ Monitoring Fabric and Connectivity Monitor tooling.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The monitoring/telemetry stack is what converts a switch sale into recurring revenue — it is the moat that survives a hardware pricing war.
insights.locator: Services revenues, thanks to the adoption of its EOS network operating system

insights.claim: Software subscriptions at Arista Networks are estimated at $137.2 million in Q2 2026, up 4.3X year on year, with software and subscriptions together at roughly $567.7 million, up 58 percent — growing materially faster than total revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A software line compounding at 4.3X inside a hardware company argues for multiple expansion — but note the company no longer breaks this composite out, so it is an estimate.
insights.locator: Our best guess is that Arista Networks had $137.2 million

insights.claim: Neoclouds, sovereign AI buyers, model builders and large enterprises cannot afford to build their own network operating systems and traffic tooling the way hyperscalers can, so they buy Arista's software along with the switches rather than assembling SONiC plus open source.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The customer mix shift away from hyperscaler 'blue box' deals toward neoclouds and sovereigns is structurally margin-accretive — software attach rides along.
insights.quote: They really have no choice, other than to grab SONiC and a bunch of open source tools, and that is not a lot of fun.
insights.locator: There may be some “blue box” deals

themes.theme: Three directions: scale up, scale out, scale across

insights.claim: Arista Networks raised its 2026 AI back end plus front end network forecast by $100 million to $3.6 billion, implying roughly 2.1X year-on-year growth in that category.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AI networking is doubling annually while the total company grows 44 percent — the mix shift toward AI is mechanical and will keep lifting the growth rate.
insights.locator: Arista Networks has boosted its forecast for AI back end and front end networks

insights.claim: Arista Networks lifted full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $1.1 billion to $12.6 billion, which would be 44 percent growth over 2025, while the campus group is still modeled at about $1.25 billion, or 53.4 percent growth.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Campus growing faster than the company average is the overlooked leg — the AI story is masking an enterprise campus share-take from incumbents.
insights.locator: The campus group is still expected to do around $1.25 billion

insights.claim: Scale across networks — those linking datacenters and regions together — will be about 30 percent of Arista's AI networking category in 2026, roughly $1.08 billion, with scale up and scale out making up the remaining 70 percent or $2.52 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Scale across is already a third of AI networking revenue — the multi-datacenter training topology is a revenue line today, not a 2028 concept.
insights.locator: Ullal, chief executive officer at the company, gave a little color

insights.claim: The scale across market is roughly $3 billion for switch gear plus $1 billion for optics in 2026, growing to about $15 billion for switching and $5 billion for optics by 2030 — implying Arista already holds a little more than a third of this emerging segment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 5X TAM expansion by 2030 in a segment where Arista already has ~35 percent share is the cleanest long-duration growth vector in the story; optics suppliers levered to DCI are the second-order play.
insights.locator: Ullal added that the scale across market in 2026

themes.theme: The NVLink displacement gate on scale up

insights.claim: Arista's scale up switching opportunity is capped by how fast customers abandon Nvidia's NVLink and NVSwitch for other XPUs or force Nvidia toward a cheaper, more standardized approach — the market cannot grow faster than that substitution.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Model Arista's scale up revenue as a function of Nvidia's share loss, not of AI capex — the two can diverge sharply.
insights.quote: But that market can only grow as fast as people stop using Nvidia’s NVLink and NVSwitch scale up networking and use other XPUs or compel Nvidia to adopt a cheaper and more standardized approach.
insights.locator: Scale up is another big opportunity

insights.claim: Nvidia is expected to end up with roughly 65 percent of the scale up networking market rather than close to 100 percent, with both customer defection to alternative XPUs and Nvidia standardizing on cheaper approaches seen as likely.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A ~35 point share transfer in scale up interconnect is the specific quantum of value up for grabs between Nvidia and the Ethernet camp.
insights.quote: (Both are likely until Nvidia ends up with maybe 65 percent of the market instead of damned near 100 percent.)
insights.locator: Scale up is another big opportunity

insights.claim: Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 Ultra switch ASIC is identified as the specific silicon through which Arista expects to attack the scale up market.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Arista's scale up upside is a direct read-through to Broadcom merchant switch ASIC volumes — the two names move on the same substitution thesis.
insights.locator: particularly in switches using Broadcom’s Tomahawk 6 Ultra switch ASIC

insights.claim: The InfiniBand-to-Ethernet transition is offered as the template for NVLink displacement: it took two to three years of talking about InfiniBand before it stopped being mentioned, so proprietary scale up should take a comparable multi-year period to erode even where Ethernet is technically good enough.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sets the clock: expect scale up Ethernet revenue to be a 2028-2029 story, so do not underwrite near-term numbers on it.
insights.quote: I feel a little bit like two or three years ago we were talking about InfiniBand and now we don't mention InfiniBand. But it took two or three years to move to Ethernet.
insights.locator: Here is how Ullal cased the situation with scale up

insights.claim: Arista expects to co-design custom racks with customers using their own custom processors in non-Nvidia accounts, tuning the network to the behavior of a specific inference or training engine.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom-silicon programs at hyperscalers pull Arista into the rack design, deepening lock-in exactly where Nvidia is weakest.
insights.quote: Where it's non-Nvidia, Arista will be excited and will be working more closely both in the scale up and scale out – in some cases to build custom racks with their custom processors
insights.locator: Here is how Ullal cased the situation with scale up

insights.claim: Arista Networks' datacenter business is modeled at $2.82 billion of Q2 2026 sales, up 37.7 percent, with $1.28 billion of operating profit, up 39.7 percent, for a 45.4 percent operating margin — well above the corporate average.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 45 percent operating margin datacenter segment means every incremental AI dollar is disproportionately accretive; margin compression would have to come from mix shift to campus, not from AI.
